Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 
SPECIFICATION FOR SPRING COLLETS 



1. Scope — Prescribes requirements for the following three types of spfing collets 

Type DL Dead-length type collets 

Type DBX Drawback type collets with external threads 

Type CON Conical type collets 

2. Terminology — The various terms of a typical type of spring collet are Illustrated in the figure shown 
below: 




LARGEST 
DIAMETER | 
OF HEAD , 



BACK REGISTER CONICAL HEAD-' 

3. Dimensions 

3.1 Dead'Ltngth Typt Collets, Type Di — See Table L 

3.1.1 Designation — A dead-iength type collet for round material having a shank diameter of 22 mm and 
bore diameter of 1 6. mm and for the use of normal accuracy work shall be designated as: 

Collet DL 22 d 16 N IS: 6238 

Note I — Symbols ' d ' for round, • /j ' for hexagon and ' $ ' for square shall be used for designating ttie dtfferent form 
of bores. 

Note! — Symbols 'N' for normal and ' P ' f f precision ( see 5 ) shall be used for designating the accuracy require- 
ments for spring collets. 

3.1.2 Finish— Collet ccnical head and bore — 60 ± 2 HRC 

Back register and body — 42 i 3 HRC 

3.2 Orawbock Type Collets with External Threads, Type DBX — See Table 2. 

3.2.1 Designation — A drlawback type collet with external threads for round material having a shank 
diameter of 50 mm and bore diameter of 20 mm and for the use of normal accuracy work shall be designated as: 

Collet DBX 50d 20 N IS : 6238 

Note I — Symbols ' d* for round, ' h ' for hexagon and ' s ' for square shall be used for designating the different forms of 
bores. 

Hote 2 — Symbols ' N * for normal and ' P ' for precision ( see 5 ) shall be used for designating the accuracy requirements 
for spring collets. 



3,2,2 Finish — Collet conical head and bore — >55 HRC 
Back register and body — 38 to 42 HRC 

3.3 Conical Type Collets, Type CON — See Tabic 3.

'The tolerance zone for d, h and s prior to slitting at n^ depends on the tolerance zone of the material or work to be gripped, 
if the user gives no details of the purpose for which the coileu are required, the collets shall conform to H7 for gripping

Hexagon and square bores shall be made to tolerance zone H7 for gripping hexagonal and square material up to tolerance 
zone hi I. 



3.3.1 'Designation — A conical type collet having a head diameter di=40 mm and bore diameter d=25 mm 
and for the use of normal accuracy work shall be designated as: 

Collet CON 40x25 N IS : 6238 
Nota — Symbols 'N* for normal and *P' for precision ( see 5 ) shall be used for designating the accuracy requirements 
for <pring collets. 

3.3.2 Finish ~ Hardness 46^2 HRC.

formance of the spring collets.

^Tolerance zon« for test mandrel shall be those of bright bars. The test mandrel shall be inserted In the .

6. Packing T- The spring collets shall be suitably packed as per the manufacturer's practice. Unground 
portion of collets shall be protected against rusting by any suitable rust preventive treatment. Ground 
portion shall be given a coating of oil or similar material to prevent rusting. 

7. Marking 

7.1 The spring collets shall be marked with the size of back register and the size of bore and the manu- 
facturer's name or trade-mark. In addition, packages shall be marked with the designation of the collet. 

7.2 Certittcation Marking — Details available with the Bureau of IndianStandards.
